The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. notes.contentHtml:
This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: CONCENTRATIONS Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations: Field and Applied Geology General Geology MAJOR INFORMATION The B.A. in Geology, General Geology Concentration is recommended for students planning a career in public service and education (e.g. government agencies, park rangers and K-12 science teaching), non-profit or non-governmental environmental organizations, or pre-environmental law. This Concentration has maximum elective flexibility to produce an experience tailored to the needs of the student. The B.A. in Geology, Field and Applied Geology Concentration is recommended for students planning to become professional geologists employed by environmental and geo-technical firms, governmental agencies, oil and mining companies, and for those students planning to pursue a graduate degree in geology. Emphasizing field and applied geology courses, and experiential learning, this program is designed to permit students to meet existing requirements for Professional Licensing. Geology majors must earn a grade of "C-" (1.7) or better in all required geology courses for those courses to satisfy the degree requirements for a B.A. degree in Geology. No more than 3 units of elective may be from supervision courses. At least 3 units of electives must be from GEOL courses. Students may not earn credit for both concentrations. ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/geological-sciences/geology-ba/ ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES Articulates as a Series Only: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible. This major expects that all laboratory courses required for the major will be completed in-person. The upper-division coursework assumes that students have broad experience conducting in-person lab work. CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS Find out more about this major here: What is the Geology Major? ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) The General Geology Concentration is similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Geology (the Field and Applied Geology Concentration is not). Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met. Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
notes.contentHtml:
CONCENTRATIONS

Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations:

  • Field and Applied Geology
  • General Geology


MAJOR INFORMATION

The B.A. in Geology, General Geology Concentration is recommended for students planning a career in public service and education (e.g. government agencies, park rangers and K-12 science teaching), non-profit or non-governmental environmental organizations, or pre-environmental law. This Concentration has maximum elective flexibility to produce an experience tailored to the needs of the student.

The B.A. in Geology, Field and Applied Geology Concentration is recommended for students planning to become professional geologists employed by environmental and geo-technical firms, governmental agencies, oil and mining companies, and for those students planning to pursue a graduate degree in geology. Emphasizing field and applied geology courses, and experiential learning, this program is designed to permit students to meet existing requirements for Professional Licensing.


Geology majors must earn a grade of "C-" (1.7) or better in all required geology courses for those courses to satisfy the degree requirements for a B.A. degree in Geology. No more than 3 units of elective may be from supervision courses. At least 3 units of electives must be from GEOL courses. Students may not earn credit for both concentrations.


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/geological-sciences/geology-ba/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

Articulates as a Series Only: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.


This major expects that all laboratory courses required for the major will be completed in-person. The upper-division coursework assumes that students have broad experience conducting in-person lab work.


CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS

Find out more about this major here:

  • What is the Geology Major?


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

The General Geology Concentration is similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Geology (the Field and Applied Geology Concentration is not).


Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
